S1.name: IT ransomware with OT-exposure uncertainty (Colonial-inspired, Mode A)
S1.description: A legacy remote account is compromised and ransomware spreads through vendor access and enterprise IT. Operators cannot tell whether the intruder also holds a foothold inside OT (modelled as an assumed probability), which is the decision problem behind a precautionary shutdown.
assumptions: Historical facts: IT-side ransomware; operations shut down as a precaution; OT not shown compromised.
Assumed: 15% chance an OT foothold already exists (uncertainty model, not a historical claim).
Assumed: ransomware impact probability 0.9 per reached IT host; 3 attempts per link.

S2.name: Hypothetical IT-to-OT propagation toward a pump controller (Mode B)
S2.description: Hypothetical: the same remote-account compromise, but the adversary pursues the control network through the IT/OT gateway, a SCADA server and a PLC to cause unsafe pump actuation. This is a simulation, not a claim about what happened in 2021.
assumptions: All traversal probabilities are assumed, not calibrated.
A control edge into a physical asset models the chance that a compromised controller causes unsafe actuation.
Isolation decided after the first alert takes effect after a response delay of 3 hops.

recommendations.explanation: E19: cutting the link Administrator Workstation -> IT/OT Gateway (DMZ) (network) reduces expected impact by 0.146 and the chance of a physical failure by 30.3 percentage points (isolation cost 1.0).

E20: cutting the link Identity Service (Active Directory) -> IT/OT Gateway (DMZ) (auth) reduces expected impact by 0.089 and the chance of a physical failure by 18.3 percentage points (isolation cost 1.0).

S3.name: Physical sabotage of remote field assets (Mode P)
S3.description: Hypothetical on-site sabotage at remote right-of-way assets: segments may rupture, the block valve may be forced closed, and a field RTU cabinet may be tampered with, giving the intruder control of downstream actuators.
assumptions: Sabotage success probabilities are assumed values loosely scaled to each site's physical-access exposure.
A ruptured segment keeps releasing product while upstream flow can still reach it (hazard exposure).
Physical isolation means closing a block valve; it reduces hazard but does not restore throughput.
